written.myAnswer: Magnetic domains are regions within a ferromagnetic material that are highly magnetized. Each acts as a small magnet with its own north and south poles.

In paramagnetic materials, atoms have a resultant magnetic field because their orbital and spin fields support one another. In diamagnetic materials, these fields cancel, so atoms have no resultant magnetic field.

Paramagnetic atoms have a resultant magnetic field, while diamagnetic atoms have no resultant field because their orbital and spin fields cancel. Ferromagnetic materials have groups of neighbouring atoms with parallel-aligned spins, forming highly magnetized domains that act as small magnets.
Ferromagnetic materials have domains that can be aligned so their magnetic effects combine, making the material a magnet. Steel retains this alignment, so it is suitable for permanent magnets.
